item.title: Kishu Ume: Japan's Finest Plums and Umeboshi — Guide
item.description: Wakayama produces the majority of Japan’s ume (Japanese plum), and its Nanko-ume variety, grown above all around Minabe, is considered the finest in the country — large, thin-skinned and fleshy, making umeboshi of exceptional quality. The plum orchards blanket the hills behind the coast, and in February the Minabe-Bairin grove erupts into what locals call ‘a million plum blossoms’, filling the valley with white flowers and scent. Beyond the blossoms, the region offers umeboshi tastings of every degree of saltiness and sweetness, plum wine, and factory visits explaining the long pickling process.
